summary: Built SignerListPage (route /contracts/:contractId/signers) with SignerListTable, AddSignerModal, SendForSignatureButton and AuditCertificateDownloadButton. The page renders the pre-send 'Add Signers' layout (IMG-4) for Contract Owners with an open Signer List, and switches to a read-only 'Signing Tracker' layout (IMG-5) once the contract has been sent/executed, including Download Audit Certificate. Role gating denies Approvers and any party outside CONTRACT_OWNER/LEGAL_REVIEWER/TENANT_ADMIN (UC7-BR-014); only CONTRACT_OWNER can add signers or send, matching UC7-BR-012/BR-013. Loading/empty/error/populated states are implemented and wired to the real signers/contract/esignature-settings endpoints — no mock data. Lint, unit tests (new SignerListPage.test.jsx, 7 cases) and build all pass; visually verified against IMG-4 and IMG-5 at 1440x900 via a local mock of this task's own endpoints (no live backend was available in this environment).

code_files.description: Typed HTTP client for GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /contracts/{contractId}/signers, POST .../signers/send and GET .../audit-certificate.
Fetches the Signer List for a contract.
Adds a signer to the Signer List.
Updates or reorders a signer; backend blocks once the first signature has been collected.
Removes a signer from the Signer List.
Fetches/downloads the audit certificate for an executed contract.
Grid of all signer fields (name, email, type, order, method, reminder frequency, status, timestamp) per UC7-GC-001/UC7-FV-005.
Add Signer form with mandatory-field and format validation (UC7-FV-001), rendered inline to match the target design.
Send for Signature control, disabled until a signer exists, surfacing the AF-005 connection-failure message.
Download Audit Certificate control, enabled only once the contract is Executed.
Route-level Signer List / Signing Tracker screen assembling the above components with role gating and loading/empty/error/populated states.
Screen-level tests: access gating, empty/populated signer list, add-signer flow, connection-failure message, audit certificate availability.

pr.title: feat(ui-gen): Signer List / Add Signers page (UC7)
pr.body:
Implements SignerListPage and its owned components (SignerListTable, AddSignerModal, SendForSignatureButton, AuditCertificateDownloadButton) for the UC6-UC7-combined module, per T-SIGNER-LIST-PAGE-UI.

- Wires GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/contracts/{contractId}/signers, POST .../signers/send and GET .../audit-certificate through a new signersService.js, with loading/empty/error/populated states and no mock fallback.
- Pre-send view matches design IMG-4 (Add Signer form + Signer List + Send for Signature); post-send/executed view matches IMG-5 (Signing Tracker with Download Audit Certificate, Sequential Signing / On Final Signature info panels).
- Role gating: only CONTRACT_OWNER can add/remove/send signers; LEGAL_REVIEWER and TENANT_ADMIN get read-only access; all other roles (e.g. Approver) are denied per UC7-BR-014.
- See blockers for judgement calls (missing endpoint for per-signer Reminder Frequency, grid-column scope vs design, and AddSignerModal being rendered inline rather than as an overlay).

blockers: Design IMG-4 shows an editable 'Reminder Frequency (days)' input on the Add Signer form, but neither AddSignerRequest nor UpdateSignerRequest declares a reminderFrequencyDays field (only SignerResponse does, as a read-only value). Per CLAUDE.md ('never add fields the DTO does not declare'), I rendered this field as a disabled, read-only display of the tenant default pulled from GET /esignature-settings instead of submitting it — it cannot be set or edited per-signer through any endpoint in this contract. This is a story-vs-contract conflict, not a missing-endpoint one.

AddSignerModal is specified by name as a 'modal' with props (contractId, onAdd), but IMG-4 shows it as an always-visible inline panel beside the Signer List, not an overlay/dialog. I kept the component name and prop shape from the contract but implemented it as an inline card to match the target design (visual fidelity is a hard requirement); no acceptance criterion specifies modal/overlay semantics, so this was treated as a naming-vs-layout nuance rather than a contradiction.

UC7-GC-001/UC7-FV-005 acceptance criteria require the Signer List grid to show Signer Email and Reminder Frequency per row, but IMG-4's compact in-progress table omits both columns (showing only Order/Name/Type/Method/Status). Per the task's rule that the story wins over the design on contradictions, SignerListTable renders the fuller column set (Order, Name, Email, Type, Method, Reminder, Status, Timestamp) in all states; IMG-5's wider 'Signing Tracker' table already matches this fuller set.

This task's relevant_endpoints only include contract-scoped signer/audit-certificate routes plus esignature-settings — there is no contract-detail endpoint listed. The contract title/status banner (shown in both IMG-4 and IMG-5) is populated via GET /api/v1/contracts/{id} (ContractResponse: id, contractName, status), which is already implemented and documented under the separate 'uc123' module in this same repo. I reused it rather than inventing a new endpoint, since CLAUDE.md permits importing/extending existing shared code across modules; ContractResponse only exposes contractName and status, so contract type/value/counterparty fields visible in the design banner are not rendered because no endpoint in either module's contract exposes them on a single-contract GET.

Before the contract has actually been sent, SignerResponse.signerStatus has no distinct 'not sent' enum value (its only pre-send value is the literal 'Sent'), yet the design shows 'Not Sent' badges for unsent signers. I infer 'not yet sent' by comparing the parent contract's status (Approved) rather than the per-signer status field, and only trust signerStatus verbatim once the contract status is Sent or Executed. This inferred mapping is called out here since the contract/DTOs do not define it explicitly.

There is no live backend in this environment, so visual verification against IMG-4/IMG-5 (and the lint/test/build checks) used a local Node mock server serving canned responses for exactly this task's own endpoints (contracts/{id}, contracts/{id}/signers, contracts/{id}/audit-certificate, esignature-settings) on VITE_API_BASE_URL — no mock/dev-fallback code was added to the app itself.

SignerListPage, SendForSignatureButton and AuditCertificateDownloadButton call useSendForSignature/useAuditCertificate directly for POST .../signers/send and GET .../audit-certificate; the context.json hooks list also names useSigningSession/useVerifyOtp/useApplySignature, which belong to the separate Signer-facing SigningPortalPage task (IMG-6/7/8) and were intentionally left out of this task's scope.
